paper_title: The State of the Art in Constraining Axion-to-Nucleon Coupling and Non-Newtonian Gravity from Laboratory Experiments
notes: Review paper compiling constraints on axion-to-nucleon coupling (g_an, with g_an=g_ap assumed) from Casimir-force, Casimir-less, magnetometer, Cavendish-type, and molecular-hydrogen experiments over m_a from 1e-10 eV to 200 eV. Results are shown only as graphical exclusion curves (Figs. 6, 8) plotting g_an^2/(4pi) vs m_a; no numerical tables are provided and individual curve values cannot be read reliably from the text. Only qualitative crossover masses are given (e.g. Casimir-less competitive up to ~0.5 eV, pressure stronger for m_a>0.9 eV, lateral for m_a>8 eV, new SiC-Casimir line stronger than lateral for m_a>17.8 eV). Coupling type is axion-to-nucleon; magnetometer sub-result explicitly refers to neutrons. Not a genuinely new single limit — it is a compilation. No DM density assumption (these are laboratory force/spin-force bounds, not haloscope). Text states gr strongest 1 ueV-1.7 meV, line 1 up to 0.5 eV, H2 above.
